nodes.title: SG-6.5 · Show the current World and wire the admin duration and limit fields
nodes.body:
Context: AdminApp (game/frontend/src/components/AdminApp.tsx) heading prints only the constant WORLD_ID, and its Duration (hours) and Max contributions per player inputs only change local state and are never sent anywhere. Desired behavior: show the World title, send the duration to POST /api/v1/admin/rounds, and disable the contribution-limit input because the backend has no endpoint for it (the limit comes from config contribution.max_per_player). Expected result: no admin field looks active while doing nothing. Why: the admin must not be misled about what they configure.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the admin is authenticated, when AdminApp loads, then the World title from GET /api/v1/worlds/{id} is displayed.
- Given the admin sets Duration to 12 and clicks Create round, when the request is sent, then POST /api/v1/admin/rounds carries world_id and duration "12h".
- Given no backend endpoint sets the contribution limit, when AdminApp renders, then the Max contributions per player input is disabled and an explanatory note is visible.
- Each behavior is covered by a frontend unit test with mocked fetch.


## Scope
- In scope: game/frontend/src/api/client.ts
- In scope: game/frontend/src/components/AdminApp.tsx
- In scope: frontend unit tests
- Out of scope: Backend changes
- Out of scope: New contribution-limit endpoint
- Out of scope: Player-facing UI
- Preserve: Token gate, Open/Close round, ExecutionPanel and 401 behavior
- Preserve: Existing tests


## Technical constraints
- Frontend only; use existing adminRequest helper
- Backend create contract: JSON body {world_id, starts_at, duration (Go duration string), base_release}


## Definition of done
- All three requirements implemented and their unit tests pass


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Admin console displays the current World title
nodes.body:
The backend serves GET /api/v1/worlds/{id} returning {id,title} (world.World). AdminApp should fetch it with a client function and display the title in the heading, falling back to WORLD_ID until loaded or on failure.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given GET /api/v1/worlds/the-boys-room returns a title, when AdminApp renders after token entry, then the heading contains that title.
- Given the world request fails, when AdminApp renders, then the heading still shows WORLD_ID and the page does not crash.


## Scope
- In scope: getWorld client function
- In scope: AdminApp heading
- Out of scope: Backend
- Preserve: Existing heading fallback text


## Technical constraints
- Public endpoint, no admin token


## Definition of done
- Title shown; fallback works


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Duration field is sent to the backend when creating a Round
nodes.body:
Add a createRound client call and a Create round button in AdminApp that posts {world_id, duration: `${durationHours}h`} with the bearer token, then reloads the current round id. Backend admin Create parses duration with time.ParseDuration.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given Duration is 12, when Create round is clicked, then a POST to /api/v1/admin/rounds is sent with JSON body world_id the-boys-room and duration 12h and a Bearer header.
- Given the create call returns 401, when it completes, then AdminApp returns to the token gate; other failures show the error message.


## Scope
- In scope: createRound client
- In scope: Create round button
- Out of scope: Backend
- Preserve: Open round and Close round buttons


## Technical constraints
- Use adminRequest; reuse handleError


## Dependencies
- R1 shares AdminApp.tsx


## Definition of done
- Request body matches backend createRoundRequest


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.body:
The backend limit comes from config contribution.max_per_player and the create-round request has no such field, so the input must be disabled and labelled as configured on the server.

- Given it renders, then a note stating the limit is set in server configuration is visible and no request carries the limit value.

- Out of scope: New endpoint
